## Problem

## Requirements

You receive an integer array `numbers[]` and a nonnegative integer `k`. Return how many distinct value pairs `(a, b)` drawn from `numbers` satisfy `b - a == k`.

- A distinct pair is counted only once per pair of values `(a, b)`, even when either value occurs multiple times in the array.
- `k` can equal `0`; for this case, count each distinct value occurring two or more times exactly once.

```
public static int countPair(int[] numbers, int k)
```

## Preparation

- LC 532, "K-diff Pairs in an Array," is the standard matching problem; LC 1, "Two Sum," uses the related lookup-pattern fingerprint.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think about using a hash set to store seen numbers, then for each number check if number + k or number - k exists to form a pair.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a set to store unique numbers, then iterate and count pairs where both a and a+k exist, ensuring each pair is counted once by only checking one direction.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

For k=0, count numbers that appear at least twice, the complexity target is O(n) time and O(n) space.

</details>
